quests.instruction: Blend the sounds together: /z/ /i/ /p/. Which word do they make?
quests.hint: Say the sounds slowly, then slide them together without stopping.
quests.explanation: /z/ /i/ /p/ blends into “zip”. A single changed sound would make “zap” or “sip”.
quests.funFact: Blending means sliding sounds together smoothly instead of saying them as separate pieces.

quests.instruction: Which sounds make the word “yam”?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and count out each sound in order.
quests.explanation: “Yam” is made of three sounds: /y/ /a/ /m/. The vowel is short a.

quests.instruction: What is the first sound you hear in “wag”?
quests.hint: Round your lips to start the word. Which sound does that?
quests.explanation: “Wag” starts with /w/, made with rounded lips.

quests.instruction: Blend /h/ /u/ /m/. Which word do you hear?
quests.hint: Keep each sound short, then push them together.
quests.explanation: /h/ /u/ /m/ makes “hum”. Only the vowel separates it from “him” and “ham”.
quests.funFact: Keep short vowels quick, almost like a hiccup, when you blend: h-u-m.

quests.instruction: Which vowel sound is in the middle of “nod”?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly. The middle sound is the one between the first and the last.
quests.explanation: “Nod” has the short o sound in the middle: /n/ /o/ /d/.

quests.instruction: What is the last sound in “cab”?
quests.hint: Say the word and stop when your lips pop closed.
quests.explanation: “Cab” ends with /b/. The three sounds are /k/ /a/ /b/.

quests.instruction: Which sounds make the word “den”?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly. Check the first, middle and last sound one at a time.
quests.explanation: “Den” is /d/ /e/ /n/. If you change the first sound you get “ten”, and changing the vowel gives “din”.
quests.funFact: Den, ten, hen, pen and men all rhyme because they share the ending -en.

quests.instruction: Blend /k/ /o/ /t/. Which word is it?
quests.hint: Listen for the round vowel in the middle.
quests.explanation: /k/ /o/ /t/ blends into “cot”, a small bed. The vowel is short o.

quests.instruction: Mia blended /m/ /u/ /g/ and named something you drink from. Which word did she say?
quests.hint: Mia’s word starts with /m/. Check the last sound to tell the two likely choices apart.
quests.explanation: /m/ /u/ /g/ makes “mug”. “Mud” ends with /d/ and “rug” begins with /r/.

quests.instruction: Which sound starts “pug”?
quests.hint: Notice the puff of air at the start. Do not get distracted by the ending.
quests.explanation: “Pug” starts with /p/ and ends with /g/. A pug is a small dog.

quests.instruction: Which short vowel sound fits in the middle of “hop”?
quests.hint: Say h-o-p. What sound sits between the two consonants?
quests.explanation: “Hop” has short o in the middle: /h/ /o/ /p/.
quests.funFact: Hop, top, mop and stop all share the same short o and the ending -op.

quests.instruction: Blend /t/ /i/ /n/. Which word do you get?
quests.hint: Say the sounds, then glue them together.
quests.explanation: /t/ /i/ /n/ makes “tin”. A tin is a metal can or box.

quests.instruction: Which sound ends “dip”?
quests.hint: Stop at the very end and listen to how your lips finish.
quests.explanation: “Dip” ends with /p/. It begins with /d/ and has /i/ in the middle.
quests.funFact: Cap and cab, rip and rib: the last sounds /p/ and /b/ differ only by the buzz in your throat.

quests.instruction: Which set of sounds is hiding inside “rub”?
quests.hint: Check all three sounds: first, middle, last.
quests.explanation: “Rub” has the sounds /r/ /u/ /b/. Changing the vowel gives “rob”, and changing the first sound gives “lub”, which is not a word.

quests.instruction: Mia blended /f/ /e/ /d/ to say a word that means “gave food to”. Which word is it?
quests.hint: Blend the three sounds, then check the first one carefully.
quests.explanation: /f/ /e/ /d/ makes “fed”. “Red” begins with /r/ and “fad” has short a.

quests.instruction: Blend /y/ /a/ /k/. Which word do you hear?
quests.hint: Blend the three sounds and listen for the last one.
quests.explanation: /y/ /a/ /k/ makes “yak”. “Yap” ends with /p/ and “yum” has short u.
quests.funFact: A yak is a large, long-haired animal that lives in the mountains of Asia.

quests.instruction: Sound out “gap”. Which list shows its sounds in order?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly. Make sure the first sound uses your voice.
quests.explanation: “Gap” starts with the voiced /g/. /k/ would give “cap”, and the vowel /e/ would give “gep”.

quests.instruction: Listen to the middle of “bun”. Which vowel sound is it?
quests.hint: Say b-u-n slowly. Which relaxed vowel do you hear?
quests.explanation: “Bun” has short u in the middle: /b/ /u/ /n/.

quests.instruction: “Jog” starts with which sound?
quests.hint: Listen to the very first sound, not the last one.
quests.explanation: “Jog” starts with /j/ and ends with /g/. Both sounds are made with your voice on.
quests.funFact: English words almost never end with the letter j. We use ge or dge instead, as in cage and badge.

quests.instruction: Which sound do you stop on when you say “beg”?
quests.hint: The first and last sounds are different. Which sound do you stop on?
quests.explanation: “Beg” begins with /b/ and ends with /g/.

quests.instruction: Blend /l/ /e/ /g/. Which word is it?
quests.hint: Keep the middle sound relaxed, then blend all three sounds.
quests.explanation: /l/ /e/ /g/ makes “leg”. Changing the vowel gives “log” or “lag”.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /s/ /a/ /d/?
quests.hint: Match each sound to a letter, one at a time.
quests.explanation: “Sad” has three sounds that match its three letters. “Said” has the vowel sound /e/, which does not match this blend.
quests.funFact: The word “said” is tricky. It does not follow the usual letter-sound rules, so you just have to remember it.

quests.instruction: Which sounds would you say if you read “lap” one sound at a time?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and tap out each sound.
quests.explanation: “Lap” is /l/ /a/ /p/. The first sound is /l/, not /r/, and the vowel is short a.

quests.instruction: What short vowel sound is hiding in “kit”?
quests.hint: Say k-i-t slowly. Which quick sound do you hear in the middle?
quests.explanation: “Kit” has short i in the middle: /k/ /i/ /t/. The K and the T are both quick consonant sounds.

quests.instruction: How many sounds do you hear in “jam”?
quests.hint: Tap one finger for each sound: /j/, then /a/, then /m/.
quests.explanation: “Jam” has 3 sounds: /j/ /a/ /m/. It also has 3 letters.
quests.funFact: Words where every letter has its own sound are the easiest to sound out.

quests.instruction: Blend /g/ /o/ /t/. Which word do you hear?
quests.hint: Say the vowel by itself first, then blend all three sounds.
quests.explanation: /g/ /o/ /t/ makes “got”. “Get” has short e and “gut” has short u.

quests.instruction: Which word has /u/ in the middle and /t/ at the end?
quests.hint: Check two things: the middle sound and the last sound.
quests.explanation: “Nut” has short u in the middle and ends with /t/. “Not” has short o and “net” has short e.

quests.instruction: Blend /w/ /i/ /n/. Which word do you hear?
quests.hint: Round your lips to start the word, then blend all three sounds.
quests.explanation: /w/ /i/ /n/ makes “win”. “Fin” starts with /f/ and “pin” starts with /p/.

quests.instruction: Which word has /z/ at the start, /a/ in the middle, and /p/ at the end?
quests.hint: Check the first, middle and last sounds one at a time.
quests.explanation: “Zap” is /z/ /a/ /p/. “Zip” has short i and “tap” begins with /t/.
quests.funFact: Zap and zip start with the same buzzing /z/ and differ only in the vowel.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same middle sound as “cot”?
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel in cot, then say each choice slowly.
quests.explanation: “Cot” and “fog” both have short o. “Fig” has short i and “fan” has short a.
